2608.25581.title: Are Concept Bottleneck Models Effective as Decision-Support Systems?
2608.25581.paper_summary: Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs) are interpretable-by-design neural networks that detect human-understandable concepts from the input and use them to generate predictions. By allowing users to inspect the concepts underlying a prediction and explore how predictions change under alternative concept configurations, CBMs have emerged as one of the most prominent approaches to supporting human-AI collaboration. However, user studies investigating their actual effectiveness as decision-support systems remain limited. We present two large-scale user studies (N participants = 705, N observations = 6,959) evaluating how concept-based explanations and user interventions on the model's concepts affect the performance of the human-AI team in two distinct binary classification tasks. Our results show that CBMs, and particularly their interactive component, can improve human-AI team accuracy relative to both unaided human performance and performance with non-interpretable AI support. However, these benefits emerge only under certain conditions: classification tasks perceived as difficult, easily identifiable concepts, and active interaction with the model. We also discuss how inaccurate concept detection may undermine users' trust in the model. Overall, this work provides practical guidance for the deployment of CBMs as effective decision-support tools.
2608.25581.paper_summary_zh: 概念瓶頸模型（CBMs）是設計上可解釋的神經網絡，能夠從輸入中檢測出人類可理解的概念並利用這些概念來生成預測。<lb/>通過允許用戶檢查預測背後的概念並探索在替代概念配置下預測如何變化，CBMs 已經成為支持人類與 AI 協作的最重要方法之一。<lb/>然而，調查其作為決策支持系統的實際有效性的用戶研究仍然有限。<lb/>我們呈現了兩項大規模用戶研究（參與者數 = 705，觀察數 = 6,959），評估基於概念的解釋和用戶對模型概念的干預如何影響人類-AI 團隊在兩個不同的二元分類任務中的表現。<lb/>我們的結果顯示，CBMs，特別是它們的互動組件，可以提高人類-AI 團隊的準確性，相較於無輔助的人類表現和使用不可解釋的 AI 支持的表現。<lb/>然而，這些好處僅在某些條件下出現：被認為困難的分類任務、易於識別的概念，以及與模型的主動互動。<lb/>我們還討論了不準確的概念檢測如何削弱用戶對模型的信任。<lb/>總體而言，這項工作為 CBMs 作為有效的決策支持工具的部署提供了實用的指導。
